answer: The orchard graph is rebuilt each epoch, which means the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the nectar audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 8 times its size, so a group of 47 keys loses far more than 47 single identities would. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the meadow checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. That is 34 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
